chunks: 4190 - And Ḥammād narrated from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام about the slaughtering done by a woman, so he said: “If they are women and there is no man with them, then the most knowledgeable of them should slaughter and mention the name of Allah over it.”
And I asked him about the slaughtering done by a boy, so he said: “When he is active, is five spans tall, and is able to handle the blade.”

key_terms.أَعْلَمُهُنَّ: the most knowledgeable among the women present
key_terms.اسْمَ اللَّهِ: the name of Allah, to be mentioned at slaughter
key_terms.الشَّفْرَةَ: the blade or knife used for slaughter
key_terms.الصَّبِيِّ: a boy whose slaughter is being assessed legally
key_terms.خَمْسَةَ أَشْبَارٍ: five spans, a measure indicating physical development
key_terms.ذَبِيحَةِ: the slaughtered animal or the act of slaughter in legal context

ai.seo_question: When is the slaughter performed by a woman or a boy considered valid in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings on who may perform slaughter in cases involving women and boys. It states that among women, the most knowledgeable one may slaughter when no man is present, and that a boy may slaughter when he has sufficient physical capability to do so.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4190 - And Hammad narrated from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as), about the slaughtering done by a woman.
Imam (as) said: "If they are women and there is no man among them, then the most knowledgeable one among them should slaughter and mention the name of Allah (swt) upon it."

And I asked Imam (as) about the slaughtering done by a boy.
Imam (as) said: "If he has reached the age where he can move, is five spans tall, and can handle the knife, then it is permissible."
